evals.prompt: Compare this branch with main and draft a PR description for me. I want to see what would go in the PR before creating it.
evals.expected_output: A well-structured Markdown PR description with Summary, What changed, and Why sections, derived from the actual git diff against main. Cross-reference syntax matches the detected platform's adapter. No PR should be created.

evals.prompt: create a PR for this branch
evals.expected_output: The skill should resolve the platform from the remote, pick an available transport, then run the full workflow: inspect state, commit and push if needed, check for existing PR, and either create a new one or return the URL of the existing one. Final output is a PR URL.

evals.prompt: necesito hacer una PR para mis cambios, y enlázala al PBI 21960
evals.expected_output: Create or update the PR (or detect the existing one) and link work item 21960 the way the detected platform's adapter says. On Azure DevOps that is the artifact-link API. If an adapter marks LINK_WORK_ITEM unsupported, it must say so and report the fallback it used instead of silently doing something different. Return the PR URL either way.

evals.prompt: crea una PR, estoy en main con cambios sin commitear que añaden un endpoint nuevo
evals.expected_output: The skill should infer the change type as 'feature' from the diff (new endpoint) without asking the user, create a feature/ branch with a short descriptive name, then continue the normal workflow: commit, push, and create the PR.

evals.prompt: revisa los comentarios de la PR de esta rama
evals.expected_output: The skill should resolve the platform, find the open PR for the current branch, and list the unresolved review threads, dropping the platform's own entries (policy, build, vote, joined-as-reviewer) per the adapter's filtering rules. The filter must be on thread state, not on who authored it: an automated reviewer's real review comments are kept, while vote and policy entries are dropped even though they carry real user identities. Each thread reported with file, line, author, and the verbatim comment. It must NOT reply to or resolve any thread without explicit approval of the exact text.

evals.prompt: revisa los comentarios de la PR de esta rama
evals.expected_output: On a PR where we already replied to a thread and the reviewer commented again: the thread must be reported as REOPENED with its round number, carrying our previous reply verbatim and everything the reviewer said after it. It must NOT be presented as a new first-time comment, and the previous reply must not be re-posted. No local ledger file is created — the history comes from the thread's own comment sequence.

evals.prompt: revisa los comentarios de la PR y arréglalos
evals.expected_output: On a thread already answered twice (round 3): report it plainly as no longer a coding problem and hand it to the human, instead of proposing a third fix. Two attempts have already missed the point, so the round number and the previous replies must be surfaced rather than another guess.

evals.prompt: revisa los comentarios de la PR de esta rama
evals.expected_output: On a PR where a thread was resolved but a later review summary links back to it with a discussionId query parameter and disputes it: the thread must appear in the fix list, flagged as reopened by citation with its round number, even though its status is Fixed and a status-filtered query does not return it. Reporting a clean list because the status filter hid it is a failure.

evals.prompt: create a PR for this branch
evals.expected_output: With a remote host that has no adapter (e.g. Bitbucket or a bare git server): stop, name the host, state that no adapter exists, and list the supported platforms. It must NOT fall back to another platform's API or guess a REST endpoint, and must NOT report a PR as created.

With a remote whose platform has an adapter but no transport available (no MCP server configured and the platform's CLI missing from PATH): stop before committing or pushing and say exactly what to install or configure, naming both routes. It must NOT fall back to a raw unauthenticated HTTP call and must NOT claim a PR was created.
